question.promptText: What is the difference between HashMap and ConcurrentHashMap, and when would you choose each?
question.referenceAnswer: HashMap is not thread-safe; concurrent structural modification can corrupt it or cause an infinite loop during resize. ConcurrentHashMap is thread-safe and uses per-bin locking (CAS plus synchronized on the first node) rather than locking the whole map, so concurrent reads are lock-free. ConcurrentHashMap forbids null keys and values because null is ambiguous with 'absent' under concurrency. Use HashMap when the map is confined to one thread or externally synchronised; use ConcurrentHashMap for shared mutable state.
